root_cause.text: In KVM’s AMD SVM nested-virtualization VMMCALL handling, L0 intercepted certain L2 VMMCALLs for Hyper-V TLB flush support but failed to synthesize a #UD when L1 had not requested VMMCALL interception, causing unsupported L2 hypercalls to be handled by L0 instead of faulting architecturally.
root_cause.evidence: The patch message says “KVM will intercept VMMCALL but never forward it to L1” and that the correct behavior is to “synthesize a #UD for VMMCALL if L2 is active, L1 does NOT want to intercept VMMCALL, nested_svm_l2_tlb_flush_enabled() is true, and the hypercall is something other than one of the supported Hyper-V hypercalls,” while the diff adds `vmmcall_interception()` to inject `UD_VECTOR` in guest mode when `!nested_svm_is_l2_tlb_flush_hcall(vcpu)` and changes `SVM_EXIT_VMMCALL` to use it.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove two unused always-false Hyper-V helper stubs from the local inline definitions.
intent_record.what: Two static inline helper functions, `kvm_hv_is_tlb_flush_hcall(struct kvm_vcpu *vcpu)` and `guest_hv_cpuid_has_l2_tlb_flush(struct kvm_vcpu *vcpu)`, were removed from the file. Both functions previously returned `false` unconditionally.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this change eliminates these two always-false helper definitions from this compilation unit, so any code expecting them here can no longer use these local stubs. Since they returned `false` for all inputs, their removal does not change the logical result on its own, but it does alter which declarations/definitions are available and may force use of a different implementation path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a helper predicate to centralize detection of nested SVM L2 TLB flush hypercalls.
intent_record.what: A new static inline helper function named nested_svm_is_l2_tlb_flush_hcall() was added. It returns the conjunction of three existing checks: guest_hv_cpuid_has_l2_tlb_flush(vcpu), nested_svm_l2_tlb_flush_enabled(vcpu), and kvm_hv_is_tlb_flush_hcall(vcpu).
intent_record.how: This adds a reusable boolean predicate that identifies when a nested SVM guest is using an L2 TLB flush hypercall, enabling later code to gate behavior on all required conditions in one place and avoid duplicating the same compound test.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a stub helper that always reports no L2 TLB flush hypercall support when KVM Hyper-V is disabled.
intent_record.what: A new static inline helper function named nested_svm_is_l2_tlb_flush_hcall(struct kvm_vcpu *vcpu) was added in the CONFIG_KVM_HYPERV-disabled code path, and it unconditionally returns false. The surrounding code remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: This provides a stub implementation for builds without KVM Hyper-V support so callers can invoke the helper safely and always receive a false result, preserving compile-time interface consistency without enabling any Hyper-V-specific L2 TLB flush hypercall behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor nested SVM VMMCALL handling to use a consolidated helper for detecting Hyper-V L2 TLB flush hypercalls.
intent_record.what: In the SVM VMMCALL exit handling path, the three-part conditional checking `guest_hv_cpuid_has_l2_tlb_flush(vcpu)`, `nested_svm_l2_tlb_flush_enabled(vcpu)`, and `kvm_hv_is_tlb_flush_hcall(vcpu)` was replaced with a single call to `nested_svm_is_l2_tlb_flush_hcall(vcpu)`.
intent_record.how: Runtime behavior is unchanged in intent but the decision of whether to treat the VMMCALL as a Hyper-V L2 TLB flush hypercall is now centralized in one helper. This makes the code use the consolidated predicate to decide whether the exit should be handled by the host.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the missing hyperv.h include so Hyper-V-related SVM code can compile with the needed declarations.
intent_record.what: A new preprocessor include directive for "hyperv.h" was added between the existing includes of "svm_ops.h" and "kvm_onhyperv.h".
intent_record.how: This makes declarations and definitions from hyperv.h available to the translation unit, which can resolve previously unavailable symbols or types needed by the surrounding Hyper-V-related code.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add nested-guest VMMCALL handling that injects #UD for unsupported L2 calls while preserving Hyper-V TLB flush hypercall emulation.
intent_record.what: A new static function named `vmmcall_interception()` was added. It checks whether the vCPU is in guest mode and whether the intercepted VMMCALL is not a nested SVM L2 TLB flush hypercall. If both conditions are true, it queues a UD exception (`#UD`) and returns 1; otherwise, it calls `kvm_emulate_hypercall(vcpu)` and returns its result. The function is inserted before the `svm_exit_handlers` table.
intent_record.how: This changes VMMCALL handling so that when L2 guest execution issues a VMMCALL that should not be treated as a Hyper-V TLB flush hypercall, KVM explicitly injects an illegal-instruction exception instead of emulating the hypercall. For allowed Hyper-V L2 TLB flush hypercalls, it preserves normal hypercall emulation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Route VMMCALL exits to the proper interception handler instead of the generic hypercall emulator.
intent_record.what: In the SVM exit handler table, the function mapped to `SVM_EXIT_VMMCALL` was changed from `kvm_emulate_hypercall` to `vmmcall_interception`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, VMMCALL exits are now dispatched to a dedicated interception handler instead of the generic hypercall emulation path, changing how that specific VM-exit is processed.

consistency_review.core_intent: Refactor nested SVM VMMCALL handling to use a consolidated helper for detecting Hyper-V L2 TLB flush hypercalls.
Route VMMCALL exits to the correct interception path, including nested-guest handling where unsupported L2 calls inject #UD while preserving Hyper-V hypercall emulation.

relevance_review.reason: The change only removes unused Hyper-V helper stubs and does not affect nested-virtualization VMMCALL interception or #UD synthesis for unsupported L2 hypercalls.

The changes target nested SVM VMMCALL handling for Hyper-V L2 TLB flush hypercalls, which is the exact area implicated by the root cause where L0 intercepted L2 VMMCALLs instead of raising #UD when L1 had not enabled VMMCALL interception.

The change is about Hyper-V L2 TLB flush hypercall support in nested virtualization, which is directly tied to the VMMCALL/hypercall handling path implicated by the bug. Even though it is a stub for the disabled case, it affects whether L2 hypercalls are considered supported and thus relates to the root cause of improperly handling unsupported L2 VMMCALLs.

This change only adds a missing Hyper-V header include for compilation. It does not alter nested SVM VMMCALL handling, interception logic, or the missing #UD synthesis described in the vulnerability root cause.

The group directly addresses the nested SVM VMMCALL bug: it changes VMMCALL exit routing and adds nested-guest handling so unsupported L2 VMMCALLs inject #UD when L1 did not intercept them, while still preserving Hyper-V hypercall emulation.

vuln_statements.explanation: This return path hands the nested VMMCALL exit back to L0 host handling. In the vulnerable flow, certain L2 Hyper-V VMMCALLs were incorrectly handled by L0 even when L1 had not enabled VMMCALL interception, instead of injecting the architectural #UD into L2.
